answer.new_information: The NVL72x2 scrapping is already held in e101 (DCD relaying SemiAnalysis), so it is the same claim. New here: SemiAnalysis reports the four-die Rubin Ultra version is canceled, leaving only the two-die version at roughly half the real-world compute performance; CPO-NVSwitch is not expected until the Feynman generation; and Nvidia plans to sell more Oberon-Rubin racks in the existing form factor. All are SemiAnalysis rumour relayed by The Decoder, with no dates for the cancellations and no Nvidia confirmation beyond 'roadmap intact' (e65, e72, e102). The record does not restate the 2028 Kyber date with a launch month, so it moves no date.

arguments.statement: Lean: Kyber NVL144 does not launch by 2027-12-31 (rung 2, unchanged). SemiAnalysis, reported by CNBC and DCD, says Kyber was delayed by more than 12 months to 2028 because the PCB midplane is hard to manufacture without defects (e64, e66, e98, e100, e101), and the same report says the NVL72x2 alternative was scrapped and the four-die Rubin Ultra version canceled, leaving only the two-die version at roughly half the real-world compute (e101 plus The Decoder record). That strengthens the case that Kyber's intended Rubin Ultra path is narrowing, not that Kyber has launched. Nvidia's denial ('roadmap is intact', e65, e72, e102) is contested and nonspecific.
limitations: SemiAnalysis rumour via CNBC and DCD; a single-source report
Delay to 2028 is a report, not a filing or shipment
The four-die Rubin Ultra cancellation and NVL72x2 scrapping have no stated date
Nvidia says its roadmap is intact but gives no specifics
what_would_change_it: Nvidia confirmation or a roadmap update naming Kyber's launch timing
Shipment or availability confirmation for Kyber NVL144 racks
Independent supply-chain confirmation of the PCB midplane problem or its resolution

arguments.statement: No lean change; the record does not settle whether Kyber launches on or before 2028-12-31. SemiAnalysis, relayed by CNBC and DCD, says Kyber is delayed to 2028 (e64, e66, e98, e101), and the new record adds that the four-die Rubin Ultra version is canceled and only the two-die version remains. A 2028 date falls within the window, but no month is given, and the cancelled four-die variant and the CPO-NVSwitch slip to Feynman add execution risk.
limitations: Delay to '2028' gives no month, so the launch could fall inside or outside 2028
Nvidia denies delay and says its roadmap is intact
what_would_change_it: Nvidia product announcement or launch date for Kyber
Shipment confirmation of Kyber racks in 2028
Confirmation or denial of the four-die Rubin Ultra cancellation

answer.reason: The record repeats SemiAnalysis's Kyber delay and NVL72x2 scrapping already held in e101 (same claim, not independent), and adds Rubin Ultra four-die cancellation and CPO-NVSwitch timing that bear on Kyber's launch path. It moves the limitations of the Kyber questions without changing any date or rung, so it updates v11 and v13 rather than proposing a new view.
